notes: The shoot opens in the mode the two of them agreed, waits for a person to plan it, and closes only when the people who were there say it happened.
her_actual_row: collab_agreements.terms_json->>'mode' = 'visit'; contracts.production_mode = NULL; production_events.mode = 'remote'; production_events.status = 'completed'. The audit log had two entries one second apart, both actor_role='system': 'Mode set to remote' and 'Remote mode auto-completed'. Nobody did anything.
fault_1_the_mode_was_thrown_away: contracts.production_mode is written in exactly ONE place — the brand's Approve & Send step — which briefing-straight-to-signing skips by design. So it was never set, and `contract.production_mode || 'remote'` invented a remote shoot on a collaboration whose agreement plainly said visit. Same fault as asking her to agree twice: settled at the handshake, re-guessed later in a different vocabulary.
fault_2_remote_was_born_completed: `mode === 'remote' ? 'completed' : 'proposed'`, reasoning that remote has nothing to coordinate. There is nothing to COORDINATE. There is still a shoot to DO. A SECOND place said the same thing — confirming a remote flip also wrote status='completed' — so fixing one would not have been enough.
what_stage_4_actually_built: Most of it shipped and works: slot proposal from either side (brand via setVisitDetails, creator via proposeSlot), counterPropose with 2 reschedules per side, getVisitDateRange with four bases, the full shipment chain, receiving-is-not-shooting, the mutual remote flip, and one shared vocabulary across both phones. NONE of it was reachable, because every transition refuses to run on a completed event and the event was created completed. Stage 4 was not missing — it was sealed shut on the first line.
the_one_thing_stage_4_got_wrong: MAY_COMPLETE = { visit: ['brand','influencer'] } is the right answer to WHO MAY MARK IT. It was read as WHO IS ENOUGH TO CLOSE IT, so the first tap from either side closed a visit the other might say never happened. Now two separately named constants: MAY_COMPLETE and REQUIRES_BOTH = ['visit']. Her mark is required in every mode — a visit closed on the brand's mark alone would be the brand reporting her work for her.
the_third_screen_state: Once both marks are needed there is a state between not-done and done: 'I have marked it, waiting for you.' Both screens had two states, so the button stayed after she tapped and tapping again did nothing — which reads as broken.
